tier_reason: Tier stays A (public lzbench 2.4 code, flags, compiler and CPU). Caveat correction: the decode deficit against xz in the same table is largely a build difference, since lzbench compiles the 7-Zip C decoder without LzmaDecOpt.asm while liblzma gets its x86-64 asm range decoder; the dictionary sizes also differ (256 MB vs 64 MiB at level 9).

corrections.caveats: lzbench lzma row: C decoder only (no Z7_LZMA_DEC_OPT), asm decoder about 1.53x faster per ip7z/7zip issue #11; lzma -9 uses a 256 MB dictionary vs xz -9's 64 MiB; decode timing includes per-call dictionary allocation and 1 MB stream-buffer memcpy; encoder needs about 2.9 GB at -9 and starts a second match-finder thread by default; raw .lzma has no checksum; win over bzip2 is off-baseline.
